anchors.5: Preserves every canon fact, connects every scene, or supplies every requested playable hook, respectively.
anchors.4: One minor omission, without contradiction or loss of playability.

briefs.prompt: Outline a three-scene session in a fishing town. Canon: The tide bell rings only at low tide. Keeper Iona has never left town. A submerged causeway links the town to an abandoned orchard. Include an investigation clue, a choice with two meaningful consequences and an ending hook. Keep the outline under 300 words.

Outline a three-scene one-shot at a glassworks. Canon: Foreman Sel has barred fire magic indoors. The night shift is paid in paper chits. The guild seal is a square with a diagonal crack. Include two noncombat solutions and an observable consequence for each. Keep the outline under 300 words.

Outline a three-scene campaign session at a stranded passenger train. Canon: The train has four carriages. The conductor can read but cannot speak. The signal tower is uphill and has no working lamp. Include an escalating complication, a choice that affects passengers, and two follow-up hooks. Keep the outline under 300 words.

Outline a three-scene campaign session about a village water dispute. Canon: The upper well is dry. The lower well is shared by three farms. A festival in two days requires no water. Include two factions with defensible goals, a clue available without negotiation and a choice with a lasting consequence. Keep the outline under 300 words.
